rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i1040gi p. 88, Line 1: "If you received a refund, credit, or offset of state or local income taxes in 2025, you may be required to report this amount", and the TIP: "None of your refund is taxable if, in the year you paid the tax, you either (a) didn't itemize deductions, or (b) elected to deduct state and local general sales taxes". With no refund received, line 1 is zero and the refund worksheet is not needed; the project guards on refund.received above zero. The candidate copies refund.line9 without that guard, so it needs worksheet answers (refund.box8) from filers with no refund. executable-triage-v2 (`reviews/2025/transcription/triage/s1.json`, written by triage.py this round; 1,495 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 639 partial records from 40 bases; 2,634 comparisons per line; completed-return witnesses listed from an uncapped scratch re-run of triage.mjs, /tmp/adj-bklg-income/full/, same counts): 1,165 of 2,634 agree; all 1,469 differences are candidate-unknown on refund.box8 with project $0.00 (124 on completed returns, all fixtures, e.g. classm.asset.1, classm.eic.1, classm.f4952.1; 862 incomplete, 483 refused). No value differences. Same expression and ruling as fix round 3; line 1 is unchanged by the backlog packages. Project stands.

Ruling: equivalent; project retained. The project gives zero when no refund was received (refund.has) and otherwise the worksheet result, zero unless you itemized for 2024 and deducted income taxes; the second gives the latter alone. With no refund, worksheet line 1 is zero (the smaller of zero and 2024 line 5d), so line 9 is zero and the two agree (i1040gi p. 90, State and Local Income Tax Refund Worksheet, line 1, "Enter the income tax refund from Form(s) 1099-G", and line 9, "Enter the smaller of line 3 or line 8 here and on Schedule 1, line 1"). The project's guard keeps the worksheet's questions and its exception screens from being asked of a filer with no refund.

Ruling: equivalent; project retained. With no qualified expenses the smaller of the expenses and $300 is zero either way; the project's guard keeps a filer without expenses from being asked whether they were an eligible educator.

Ruling: model error; i1040gi p. 93, Line 16: "If you were self-employed or a partner, you may be able to take this deduction". Partnership and other Schedule E or K-1 income is refused by scope.schedule1, so within scope only a person with a Schedule C can have the deduction; the project asks person.plan only then (person.s16, guarded by person.has_sc). The candidate sums person.plan_deduction for every person, asking plan questions of people with no self-employment income and reaching the SEP and SIMPLE excess screens for them. executable-triage-v2 (`reviews/2025/transcription/triage/s1.json`, written by triage.py this round; 1,495 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 639 partial records from 40 bases; 2,634 comparisons per line; completed-return witnesses listed from an uncapped scratch re-run of triage.mjs, /tmp/adj-bklg-income/full/, same counts): 1,224 of 2,634 agree; 1,243 candidate-unknown on person.plan and 167 candidate-refuses (sep_excess, simple_excess), project $0.00 in every one. On completed returns: 39 candidate-unknown and 60 candidate-refuses (21 sep_excess, 39 simple_excess: e.g. classm.f8880.2, holding person[taxpayer].plan simple with no Schedule C; classm.s2.3, classm.f1040.5, classm.clcw26.2, classm.f5329.1, classm.f8889.1, classm.sli.3, stage21.t067.smw_hidden_ira, stage21.f1.lower_bound_still_decides and generated 49, 80, 86, 90, 135, 143, 174, 175, 181, 199, 208, 236, 255, 259, 290, 361, 363, 366, 367, 381, 399, 401, 439, 453, 477, with partials), each with a plan answer for a person the interview never asks. No value differences. Same expression and ruling as fix round 3. Project stands.

Ruling: representation; i1040gi p. 98, IRA Deduction Worksheet, line 12: "Add the amounts on lines 12a and 12b and enter the total on Schedule 1, line 20". The candidate's ira.line12a plus ira.line12b is the same total of person.ira_deduction over you and your spouse as the project's ira.total. executable-triage-v2 (`reviews/2025/transcription/triage/s1.json`, written by triage.py this round; 1,495 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 639 partial records from 40 bases; 2,634 comparisons per line; completed-return witnesses listed from an uncapped scratch re-run of triage.mjs, /tmp/adj-bklg-income/full/, same counts): 2,605 of 2,634 agree; no value differences and no difference on a completed return. The 22 candidate-unknown (21 incomplete, 1 refused; e.g. stage16.ira.i1 to i10, stage16.mut.ira_kbh_one_edge, audit.ira.covered_age50_single_phaseout, ss.person.separation) stop inside person.ira_deduction on modified AGI, which the candidate builds from its own Schedule 1 lines (line 1 needing refund.box8, ruled above, and the ungated refusal declarations on lines 2a and 19a that read s1.alimony_unsupported on every return); the 7 project-refuses (stage16.refuse.ira.kbh_short, .over_comp, .special, .excluded_income, .combat_pay, .dist, .deduct_less) are the IRA worksheet gates inside person.ira_deduction, which the candidate reaches too once those answers exist. Same expression and ruling as fix round 3. Project stands.

Ruling: equivalent within valid inputs; project retained. The amount repaid is part of a 2025 overpayment of the compensation received, so it never exceeds it and the floor at zero does not apply; with no unemployment compensation both give zero, and the project's guard keeps a filer without it from being asked about repayments.

Ruling: model error; i1040gi p. 89, Line 7: "You should receive a Form 1099-G showing in box 1 the total unemployment compensation paid to you in 2025. Report this amount on line 7", reduced by contributions ("If you made contributions to a governmental unemployment compensation program and you aren't itemizing deductions, reduce the amount you report on line 7 by those contributions") and by 2025 overpayments repaid. With no compensation paid in 2025, line 7 is zero and neither s1.uc_repaid nor the s1.uc_unsupported screen is needed; the project asks both only when s1.has_uc (s1.uc_paid above zero). The candidate drops that guard and declares the screen on every return. executable-triage-v2 (`reviews/2025/transcription/triage/s1.json`, written by triage.py this round; 1,495 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 639 partial records from 40 bases; 2,634 comparisons per line; completed-return witnesses listed from an uncapped scratch re-run of triage.mjs, /tmp/adj-bklg-income/full/, same counts): 1,330 of 2,634 agree; 1,258 candidate-unknown (s1.uc_unsupported and s1.uc_repaid) and 46 candidate-refuses on s1.uc_unsupported, project $0.00 in every one. On completed returns: 140 candidate-unknown and 10 candidate-refuses; the refusals are classm.f1040.6, classm.f1040.6.deepseek, classm.f5695.2.deepseek and seven partials of those bases, each holding s1.uc_unsupported true with s1.uc_paid $0, an answer the interview never asks (the tooling package's PENDING-2 notes such off-route generator answers remain in class M cases until each is regenerated). No value differences. The income package changed only the wording of s1.uc_unsupported (PENDING-2: payments a self-employed filer made for elective coverage now count, only tax an employer paid on wages is excluded, as i1040gi p. 89, Line 7, "If you made contributions to a governmental unemployment compensation program") and of the alimony questions (PENDING-1 and PENDING-3, p504 pp. 15-16); no s1 expression changed, and no wording change widens a computed case. Project stands.

Ruling: model error; i1040gi p. 91, Line 8c: "Enter any canceled debt. Canceled debt may be shown in box 2 of Form 1099-C. However, part or all of your income from cancellation of debt may be nontaxable. See Pub. 4681". The value is the project's (zero without canceled debt, the amount with it), but the reply's line declares `refuses: [s1.cod_unsupported]` without a guard, so it needs the exceptions-and-exclusions screen on every return; the project asks it only when s1.cod_any is true and the amount is positive (s1.cod_refused; amb.2025.cod_fully_taxable). executable-triage-v2 (`reviews/2025/transcription/triage/s1.json`, written by triage.py this round; 1,495 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 639 partial records from 40 bases; 2,634 comparisons per line; completed-return witnesses listed from an uncapped scratch re-run of triage.mjs, /tmp/adj-bklg-income/full/, same counts): 1,145 of 2,634 agree; all 1,489 differences are candidate-unknown on s1.cod_unsupported with project $0.00 (137 on completed returns, the same 124 fixtures as line 1 plus generated returns and partials; 861 incomplete, 491 refused). No value differences. Project stands.

Ruling: equivalent; project retained. The project asks first whether any debt was canceled (s1.cod_any, the owner's answer to Stage 16 question 13) and asks the amount only on a Yes; with no canceled debt both give zero, and with some both give the amount (i1040gi p. 91, Line 8c; p525 p. 20, Canceled Debts, "If the debt is a nonbusiness debt, report the canceled amount on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 8c"). A Yes with a zero amount gives zero in both. The project's guards place the exceptions-and-exclusions refusal (s1.cod_unsupported, on s1.cod_refused) only on a return that has canceled debt.

Ruling: equivalent; project retained. With no canceled debt both give zero; with some, both give the amount (i1040gi p. 91, Line 8c; p525 p. 20, Canceled Debts, "If the debt is a nonbusiness debt, report the canceled amount on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 8c"). The project's guard places the exceptions-and-exclusions refusal (s1.cod_unsupported, on s1.cod_refused) only on a return that has canceled debt.

Ruling: ambiguity; i1040gi p. 92, Line 8z: "Use line 8z to report any taxable income not reported elsewhere on your return ... For more details, see Miscellaneous Income in Pub. 525". The candidate sums oi8z.amount for every kind, refusing only recoveries, a corrective-distribution loss and charitable recapture; the project sums oi8z.taxable, which also refuses kinds whose taxable part needs other rules (corrective distributions, disaster relief, insurance dividends, any other kind) through oi8z.figured, the owner's choice amb.2025.line8z_kinds (decision D4). Triage executable-triage-v1 (triage/s1.json): 2,187 of 2,210 agree; all 23 differences are project-refuses on oi8z.figured where the candidate computes the entered amount (classm.dependent.3: kind other, candidate $6,999.00; stage16.refuse.oi8z.figured: $2,300.00; generated 0, 28, 39, 50). Project stands.

Ruling: model error; i1040gi p. 91, Line 8b: "Enter gambling winnings not attributable to a trade or business"; p525 p. 33, Gambling winnings: "If you're in the trade or business of gambling, use Schedule C (Form 1040)". The test itself is the project's (line 8b is a copy of s1.gambling_winnings, so line 8b above zero and winnings above zero are the same test), but the reply's line 8b declares `refuses: [s1.gambling_pro]` with no guard, so its test needs the professional-gambler answer on every return; the source and the project need it only when there are winnings (gate s1.gambling_business = has_gambling and gambling_pro). A candidate that needs an answer the source does not need is a model error (README). executable-triage-v2 (`reviews/2025/transcription/triage/s1.json`, written by triage.py this round; 1,495 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 639 partial records from 40 bases; 2,634 comparisons per line; completed-return witnesses listed from an uncapped scratch re-run of triage.mjs, /tmp/adj-bklg-income/full/, same counts): 1,156 of 2,634 agree; 1,477 candidate-unknown on s1.gambling_pro (137 on completed returns: 124 fixtures, among them classm.asset.1, classm.eic.1, classm.f1095a.1, classm.f4952.1 and .2, classm.f5695.1, .2, .7 and .9, classm.f8962.1 to .3, plus generated returns and partials; 853 incomplete, 487 refused) and 1 candidate-refuses on a refused return. Every witness has project $0.00 (or false); no value difference on any record. Project stands.
